text.p: The International Air Services Commission said on Thursday it would renew Qantas Airways Ltd's allocation of one service a week to South Africa for five years.
The commission said this was the first of a large number of determinations expiring on June 30, 1997, to be renewed.

The commission, Australia's air services regulator, also said it had issued a draft determination proposing to renew Qantas' equivalent of 1.8 B747 flights per week to Malaysia and the equivalent of 7.6 B747 services per week to Indonesia.
Draft determinations for the renewal of Qantas' unlimited passenger and freight capacity to New Zealand was also being considered, the commission said.
The closing date for submissions on the draft determinations will close on November 15.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
